Manipulate the setup menus. Parameter A consists of zero or more characters from the set "oqudlrse0123456789", followed by a terminating line feed, semi-colin or null. Note that the effect of a specific string depends on the current state and software version - do not rely on specific string sequences to always have the same effect. The commands are: 'o' - open setup menu, 'q' - quit setup menu, 'u' - up, 'd' - down, 'l' - left, 'r' - right, 's' - select, 'e' - back, '0' to '9' - 0 to 9.

Manipulate the video adjustment menu or color bar according to n where n is 'u'=up, 'd'=down, 'l'=left, 'r'=right, 'e'=back, 's'=select, 'q'=quit, 'f'=bar on and 'o'=menu on. Note that 'f' and 'o' will turn off the video adjustment menu, color bar, the logo and the status lines before turning the color bar or video menu on. Note that 'e' and 's' do not work with the color bar. The other commands are only valid when the video adjustment menu or color bar is on. These commands are only valid on an AVM 50 or a Statement D2.

The SC commands are used to change the parameters that are in the "ADJUST INPUT LEVELS" menu and the "SOURCE SETUP" sub-menus. Parameter "a" must be "AD" or must be a single letter given in the following commands. Parmeter "n" specifies which source setup menu. Set gamma table x { = 0- single table, = 1 Red table, =2 Green table, =3 Blue table} table entry number ZZ { hexadecimal (0 – 1E (30D)) } to (XXX ,YYY). XXX and YYY are the X and Y values of the point in hexadecimal (0 – 3FF). 
Note that each curve must start with a point with XXX = 000, and finish with XXX = 3FF. After you are done making changes to a curve you must send a point just after the last valid point (just after the one with an XXX value of 1023) with an XXX and YYY value of AAA to mark the curve as valid, resulting in a recalculation of the gamma table.
Example: assume unit has already been configured with 20 gamma points, sending: fIs00A2FF2AF;fIs014AAAAAA; will set the point at 0A(11th point) in the single table to a value of (2FF,2AF) and then trigger re-calculation of the gamma table.
It is up to the user to ensure that all points are in order. (the XXX values must be in increasing values as the point # (ZZ) increases). - No sorting is done on the entries.

Querry gamma table x, entry # ZZ. Returns fIxZZXXXYYY. (see above)
To determine the number of valid points in a specific table you must querry each value (from 0 - 1E) the first point with invalid values (>3FF, AAA is prefered 'invalid' value) is the number of valid points.
